doc: judge_surface(ref, maps): one row per judged metric (SURFACE_JUDGED order, params.judged; inputs hold the columns params.keys: the six judged ones then the two season terms). v = the metric over the maps; spread = sample std (ddof 1; NaN for one map); season = |ref[season term]| or 0; tolerance = max(2.2 * spread, floor) + season with floor 2.5 for itcz_lat and 0.01 otherwise; diff = mean(v) - ref; pass = tolerance finite and |diff| <= tolerance. Python max(nan, floor) is NaN (the first argument wins when a comparison fails): do not port it as floor. Float64 arithmetic on a handful of numbers: 1e-9; no verdict sits within 1e-6 of a tie, except in exact_ties and just_over_ties, which sit ON one (or an ulp past it) by construction, from exactly representable operations. Two IDENTICAL maps (spread exactly 0; the mean of two equal floats is exact), so tolerance = floor + season allowance with no spread term, and a reference of 0 (8.0 for itcz_lat) so that diff is the map value itself, in exact float64 arithmetic: land_minus_ocean 0.01 against the floor 0.01; subtropics_land_minus_ocean -0.01 (the negative side: abs); north_minus_south 0.01 + 0.5 against 0.01 + |-0.5| (the season term of ocean_north_minus_south); midlat_north_minus_south -(0.01 + 0.25) against 0.01 + 0.25; itcz_lat 10.5 - 8.0 = 2.5 against its floor 2.5 (dyadic, exact); deck_minus_open -0.01 against 0.01. Every |diff| EQUALS its tolerance bit for bit: the verdict is `<=`, so all six pass (an exclusive comparison fails all six). Every operation is a single IEEE addition, subtraction, abs or an exact mean, so the tie is portable.
